findings.issue: C-B3 is violated on a P0 headline scan, and the justification comment is factually wrong. `lrs_standard` is extended by TWO half-decade points downward (1e-5, 3e-5) but only ONE upward (3e-1), contrary to the brief's "extend that edge by two half-decade points". The comment says the top extension is "to keep SGD/SGDm off the top edge (they sit on it in the MLP scans)" - but on this scan SGD's optimum is 0.001 (deep interior) and it is RMSprop that sits on the old 1e-1 top edge. From the 290 legacy jsonl in /n/labstore01/LABS/anon_lab/Users/anon/sven_experiments_legacy_2026-09-18/cifar10_resnet_ce_scan, seed-mean final val loss: RMSprop 1e-4 -> 2.1002, 1e-3 -> 1.3324, 1e-2 -> 1.3725, 1e-1 -> 1.1983 (best = top edge, by a clear margin). Adam is interior (1e-2 -> 1.2156 vs 1e-1 -> 1.3274), SGD interior (1e-3). grid_counts.md asserts "bench/best_configs.json has no CIFAR entry at all" and stops there; the raw per-run records were available and were not consulted, so the only two scans where a run costs ~0.5 GPU-h got their extension round sized from the MLP scans' evidence instead of their own.
findings.suggested_fix: Add 1.0 to `lrs_standard` in both CIFAR headline configs (+40 runs/scan = 8 standard optimizers x 5 seeds, ~0.5 GPU-h/scan at the probe's 24 ms/step and T=3.85) and rewrite the comment to name RMSprop-on-CE as the top-edge case. Also add ('cifar10_resnet_ce_scan','lrs_standard',[3e-1,1.0]) to MUST_CONTAIN in tests/test_configs.py so the reason is pinned. Since CONTRACTS.md budgets no second extension round, this is the only chance to bracket it.

findings.issue: An unaddressed and unreported C-B3 grid edge on a P0 headline scan: `lrs_lbfgs` was not extended on any scan, and on cifar10_resnet_scan_labelRegression the L-BFGS optimum IS the 1.0 top edge. From the legacy records (45 runs per lr = 3 max_iter x 3 history x 5 seeds), seed-mean final val loss: lr 0.1 -> 3.0635, 0.5 -> 0.7855, 1.0 -> 0.7534. C-B3 in CHANGES_NEEDED.md explicitly covers baselines as well as Sven, and the report's "Deviations" and "Open questions" sections do not mention the L-BFGS lr grid at all - so unlike the CIFAR-label-reg Sven lr (deviation 1, properly disclosed with a Gauss-Newton argument), this edge is simply invisible to the orchestrator. On CIFAR-CE L-BFGS is interior (best 0.5), so this is label-reg only.
findings.suggested_fix: Either extend `lrs_lbfgs` to [0.1,0.5,1.0,2.0] on cifar10_resnet_scan_labelRegression (+45 runs ~3 GPU-h; two points ~6 GPU-h) or, if the budget says no, record it as an explicit accepted edge in campaign/grid_counts.md "Open items" next to the Sven-lr item, with the seed-mean numbers above as the evidence.

findings.issue: The C-X1 config comment states the grid "contains lr * kappa/2 for every (kappa, lr) pair in it". That is false, and the acceptance test is written weakly enough to pass anyway. With lrs [0.1,0.25,0.5,0.75,1.0] and kappa {1,2,3} the realised effective steps 2*lr/kappa are {0.2,0.5,1.0,1.5,2.0}, {0.1,0.25,0.5,0.75,1.0} and {0.0667,0.1667,0.3333,0.5,0.6667}; the intersection of all three is exactly {0.5} (kappa=1 lr=0.25, kappa=2 lr=0.5, kappa=3 lr=0.75). So only 1 of the 15 (kappa, lr) points is matched across all three kappas, and for (kappa=1, lr=0.1) the required 0.05 is not in the grid at all. At k=64=B - half the 150 runs - F29's "the kappa scan is an lr sweep in disguise" therefore still applies to 14 of 15 points; only the k=32 slice, where truncation binds, genuinely separates kappa from the step. tests/test_configs.py:482-483 quotes the "at minimum include lr * kappa / 2" requirement in its docstring but then asserts only `matched` (non-empty), i.e. that at least one lr matches, which cannot fail for any grid containing a 2:1 ratio.
findings.suggested_fix: Either make the claim true - e.g. lrs [0.1,0.15,0.2,0.3,0.45,0.5,0.75,1.0] or a kappa-indexed `lrs` per arm - or correct the comment to say that one matched effective-step triple (0.5) plus the k=32 truncating slice is what the study rests on. Then strengthen the test to assert the matched set explicitly (e.g. that {0.25,0.5,0.75} all give 2*lr/kappa == 0.5 at kappa 1/2/3) rather than `assert matched`.

findings.issue: The "HIG lr >= 0.5 always crashes" rationale - repeated in four configs, in tests/test_configs.py::test_hig_grid_is_shifted_down_not_grown ("guaranteed failures") and in tests/test_grid.py:246 ("Those 40 ids are the crashing half of the old grid") - is contradicted by the data for the one scan where it is asserted as an oracle. In the legacy results, mnist_scan_ce has 20/20 finite HIG runs at lr=0.5 and 20/20 at lr=1.0; they completed and are on disk, they are simply worse than the lr=0.05 optimum. The claim does hold for toy_1d_scan, polynomial_scan and mnist_scan_labelRegression, which have zero records at lr >= 0.5. The decision to shift the grid down is right (HIG's optimum is the 0.05 bottom edge on both MNIST scans, and tau's is the 1e-2 top edge on 3 of 4 MLP scans - both claims verified), but `_explain_mnist_scan_ce` is the golden-test comment a future auditor will read to learn why 40 ids vanished, and it names the wrong reason for the wrong scan.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the rationale to what the data supports: "lr >= 0.5 produced no results at all on toy/polynomial/MNIST-label-reg and is dominated by lr=0.05 on MNIST-CE (seed-mean val 0.1035 at lr 0.05/tau 1e-2 vs nothing better above 0.1), so the grid moves down rather than outward." Fix the docstring of _explain_mnist_scan_ce in tests/test_grid.py:243-251 (integrator's file - list it in the report as you did the other five edits).

findings.issue: `strip_post_legacy` removes `_bnbatch`/`_bnfrozen` from every NEW run_id, unconditionally and for every case, before comparing against the pinned legacy enumeration. The strip is genuinely necessary (the pinned runner cannot read `bn_mode`, so it emits its own default once `gram_freeze_norm_stats` is deleted from the CIFAR configs), but it destroys the only oracle that proved the CIFAR svd ids are unchanged - and it makes the script report `OK` for a config that set the WRONG bn_mode. If someone flips a CIFAR headline scan to `bn_mode: frozen` (which would silently un-fix the ~28%-accuracy BN collapse the comment warns about), every id would gain `_bnfrozen`, the strip would remove it, and the script would still print `OK ... order_identical=True`. The `assert not n_bn` guard only fires for the two FREEZE scans, neither of which uses bn_mode.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the blanket strip with an expected-token map, e.g. EXPECTED_BN_TOKEN = {"cifar10_resnet_scan_labelRegression": "_bnbatch", "exp_finetune_cifar_smallN": "_bnfrozen"}, strip only that scan's token and assert that every id which should carry it does (and that no other scan carries any). That keeps the order/shard comparison working while still failing on a wrong-direction bn_mode.

findings.issue: The tentative Fig-5 set point is guarded by a comment only. tests/test_configs.py asserts nothing about k_values/lrs/rtol for this scan, and campaign/plan_campaign.yaml's `p1_cifar_fig5` item is enabled, so a P1 launch will run all 15 runs (~5.5 GPU-h) on the pre-Gram classic values k=64/lr=1.0/rtol=1e-3 while EXPERIMENTS.md documents k=128/lr=0.1/rtol=1e-4 for the same figure. The report lists this as open question 2 and says "nothing enforces re-pointing" - which is exactly the gap a cheap acceptance test in the owned test file could close, and this is a headline figure, so the failure mode is a wrong Fig-5 rather than a small waste.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a test to tests/test_configs.py that fails while the set point is tentative: assert the header still contains the "STILL TENTATIVE" marker AND that the plan item for this scan is `enabled: false`, so the two can only be flipped together. (Or assert k/lr/rtol equal a value recorded in a small `campaign/setpoints.yaml` that the reconcile step writes.)

findings.issue: Both CIFAR headline configs still carry `lrs_jd`, `lrs_hig` and `tau_hig` (20 JD + 80 HIG = 100 enumerable runs each), while campaign/grid_counts.md prints "-" for those families and excludes all 200 runs from the 15,953 total that the launcher is told to treat as ground truth. tests/test_configs.py::test_every_mode_the_config_carries_expands actively asserts that CIFAR's jd and hig modes enumerate non-empty, i.e. blesses them. Nothing submits them today (plan_campaign.yaml's p3_cifar_jd_hig items are `enabled: false`), but tests/test_grid.py runs this scan at mode="all" and keeps jd:20/hig:80 in INVENTORY, so a single `mode=all` job - under `scheduler=claims`, where every process expands the full grid for its mode and claims what it finds - would claim 200 unbudgeted runs. By the plan's own note HIG on ResNet18 needs a full per-sample Jacobian, ~50 GPU-h per scan.
findings.suggested_fix: Since the configs track owns these files and the scans are out of scope, delete the three keys from both CIFAR configs (grid.mode_flags then reports jd/hig as not carried, so mode=all is safe by construction) and drop the jd/hig rows from INVENTORY. If they must stay for a possible revival, at least make grid_counts.md state the 200-run liability in the per-scan table rather than only in prose.

findings.issue: Comment says "the five scans that inherit another config and override nothing", but the track added two more, so TIMING_ALIASES now has seven entries (the two new CIFAR timing configs).

`eval_batch_size: 256` is an unmeasured guess (the report says so) and is probably unnecessary. The scan is char-level: dataset shakespeare_char (CharTextDataset), model nanogpt with block_size 128, n_embd 128, so vocab is ~65 and a 2048-block eval batch is ~68 MB of logits, not an OOM. The override costs nothing (the 10% val split is ~870 blocks, so 4 eval batches instead of 1), but test_eval_batch_size_is_overridden_only_for_gpt_style_models hardcodes `ebs < 2048` for every lm_ce scan, which turns the guess into a requirement that a future BPE-tokenised or larger-vocab LM scan would inherit for the wrong reason.
findings.suggested_fix: Either measure it once and record the number in the comment, or drop the override and relax the test to `ebs <= 2048` with the rationale "an LM scan may cap it".
